callPoints: Domestic +5.4% (Apr-May +13%, then a fire at a supplier cost ~13,900 vehicles of June production, mostly Creta); exports -19.6% on the West Asia conflict. Most of the lost output was recovered in July; all of it within Q2.

EBITDA margin 9.3% (-400bp YoY): lost high-margin volume, weak exports, commodities (~100bp QoQ, ~200bp YoY: precious metals, copper), Pune stabilisation costs; partly offset by three price rises in CY26 (~100bp in all) and a weaker rupee. Discounts 2.8% of price vs 3.4% a year ago.
Guidance kept: domestic and export volume growth of 8-10% and an EBITDA margin of 11-14% for FY27. 'Comfortable is not the word... we will take actions as and when required' (MD, on margins).

Two new nameplates in H2FY27: an ICE mid-SUV (4.0-4.4 m, 'technology-first', positioned apart from the Creta; launched in the festive season) and the first mass-market dedicated EV (a localised compact SUV, aiming for PLI eligibility from day one).
Pune third shift from Oct-2026, about two years early (Pune potential 170k a year on three shifts); Chennai Plant 1 utilisation 72% in CY26, 90-92% expected in CY27 with the new models.
Industry: H1 strong on the low pre-GST base; H2 growth 'low single digits'; FY27 6-9%. HMIL aims to beat the industry in H2 and exit FY27 above its FY26 share of ~12.3%.
Rural share a record 25.9% (rural +23%, urban +2.8%); SUVs 70% of domestic volume; CNG 18.2%; localisation 83% (90% target by 2030); expects no CAFE-II penalty for FY23-FY27.

guidance.said: Growth of 8-10%, with capacity to go beyond that if demand allows.
Growth of 8-10% despite an 'extremely uncertain' environment (FY26: +16.4% vs 7-8% guided).
About Rs7,500 cr in FY27, the highest ever: Pune Phase 2 and Chennai upgrades.
Pune 250k by CY28, then +70k to ~320k; total >1.1 mn by 2030.
guidance.outcome: Pune third shift brought forward to Oct-2026.

guidance.said: Two all-new nameplates in FY27: a localised compact EV SUV and an ICE mid-SUV.
Exit FY27 above the FY26 share of ~12.3%; beat industry growth in H2.
guidance.outcome: To be seen (Q1 share ~11% on the fire).

timeline.event: Hyundai Motor India incorporated in Chennai as a wholly owned subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Company (HMC).
Second Chennai assembly plant; Chennai capacity now 824,000 a year (AR FY26).
Creta launched; becomes India's best-selling mid-SUV.
Talegaon (Pune) plant acquired from General Motors (AR FY26); re-equipped for ~Rs6,986 cr.
~Rs15,400 cr of dividends paid to HMC before the IPO (reserves fell by Rs9,389 cr despite Rs6,060 cr of profit; financing outflow Rs15,930 cr): net worth falls from Rs20,055 cr to Rs10,666 cr.
IPO: HMC sells 14.22 cr shares (17.5%) at Rs1,960, Rs27,859 cr, India's largest IPO; pure offer for sale, no new money for the company. Subscribed 2.37x.
Listed at Rs1,934 on NSE, 1.3% below the issue price.
GST 2.0: small cars 28% to 18%; larger SUVs to 40% (no cess).
Pune plant starts production (Venue), adding 170,000 of capacity.
Tarun Garg becomes HMIL's first Indian MD & CEO, succeeding Unsoo Kim.
Fire at a supplier: ~13,900 vehicles of production lost.
Bayon mid-SUV named (14-Sep) and bookings opened (23-Sep); festive launch.

fy26.contingent: CCI penalty of Rs420.3 cr (spare parts / dealer practices; enforcement subject to a Madras High Court writ appeal) and a separate Rs87 cr CCI penalty under appeal; GST compensation-cess demand of Rs258.7 cr plus an equal penalty on certain SUVs (stayed by the Madras High Court); excise demand of Rs357.4 cr plus an equal penalty; draft income-tax assessments of Rs172.9 cr pending before the DRP.
fy26.board: MD & CEO Tarun Garg (since 1-Jan-2026; first Indian MD); whole-time directors Wangdo Hur (CFO), Dong Huwy Park (COO) and Gopalakrishnan C.S. (Chief Manufacturing Officer); independent directors Ajay Tyagi, Sree Kirat Patel, Shalini Puchalapalli and John Martin Thompson. Auditor: BSR & Co. LLP.
